name: Geometric Tools
listed_description: C++ library for computing in the fields of mathematics, graphics, image analysis and physics.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. The official site www.geometrictools.com (source of the PDF write-ups) is EGRESS_BLOCKED here, so those documents could not be read. In the GitHub repo (Boost-1.0, 1.4k stars) README.md has no benchmark text; GTE/Samples/Mathematics sources (SymmetricEigensolver3x3Console.cpp, RootFindingConsole.cpp, PartialSumsConsole.cpp) test correctness only with no timing; 26 GTE/Mathematics headers fetched and grepped (SymmetricEigensolver3x3.h, BSNumber.h, ConvexHull3.h, Delaunay3.h, RootsPolynomial.h, Matrix.h and others) contain no benchmark or faster-than claims against Eigen, GMP, CGAL or Boost (only a note in BSNumber.h that an option is 'a faster alternative' to another mode of itself). Web searches for GTE versus Eigen, GMP, CGAL, Boost.Multiprecision and Boost.Geometry found no third-party timing that includes GTE.

name: giflib
listed_description: Library for reading and writing gif images
reason: giflib appears only as the baseline that others beat, never as a claimed winner. SourceForge page and NEWS have no benchmark text. The only numbers found are in google/wuffs doc/benchmarks.md (libgif 5.1.9 as the 'mimic' baseline, Intel i5-10210U, clang 11 and gcc 10, Sept 2022): Wuffs decodes 1.9x to 6.6x faster than libgif, and the Go image/gif and Rust gif 0.11.4 rows against libgif are mixed (for example MB/s libgif vs Go: 1k_color_full_init 90 vs 63, 10k_indexed 105 vs 92, but 100k_artificial 165 vs 202 and anim_screencap 199 vs 237; libgif vs Rust: 10k_indexed 105 vs 101, 1k_bw 173 vs 362, anim_screencap 199 vs 513). No source claims giflib is faster than a named implementation, and picking the Go rows it wins would be cherry-picking. The catalog already holds giflib-turbo (a giflib-compatible faster fork, wave 10).

name: GMTL
listed_description: Graphics Math Template Library is a collection of tools implementing Graphics primitives in generalized ways.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. The project page https://ggt.sourceforge.net/ only calls GMTL 'a fast and flexible base for any modern graphics project' (directional claim, no numbers) and the SourceForge project page (LGPL-2.0, last update 2013-10-13, inactive) carries no benchmark. GLM, Eigen and DirectXMath benchmark repos found by search (Math-Library-Test, vectormathbench, BenchmarksCPP) do not include GMTL.

name: GNU SASL
listed_description: Implementation of the Simple Authentication and Security Layer (SASL) framework
reason: No performance claim at all. README.md, NEWS (52 KB) and doc/gsasl.texi (105 KB) from gitlab.com/gsasl/gsasl were fetched and grepped for faster, speed, performance, benchmark, Cyrus and slower: the only hits are about integration tests, 'It's small' as a design goal (no numbers) and a manual note that one of its own password-handling approaches 'will be faster' than the other (internal comparison, no numbers). The GNU project page www.gnu.org is EGRESS_BLOCKED here.

name: gnulib
listed_description: Collection of common GNU code. Various licenses, all open source.
reason: No numeric comparison against a named external baseline. The 7.5 MB ChangeLog (through 2026-10-06), NEWS and the tests/bench-*.c sources were grepped. Quantified claims are only self-comparisons in commit messages: rawmemchr 6x faster on CHERI Morello versus the module's own earlier one-byte-read code, fts_build about 4% faster for rm -rf with 1M entries, dfa charclass struct about 5% faster for grep -Fi, a localeinfo bug fix making LC_ALL=C grep -Fw 40x faster than its own regression. tests/bench-pagealign_alloc.c compares allocation strategies of gnulib's own pagealign_alloc across OSes as percentages of memory, not time; bench-crc, bench-md5 and bench-sha*.c carry no result tables. The repo README has no benchmark section.
